sections.heading: Basecamp limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Not a deep Work OS / portfolio planner; Minimal native automation; Free limited to one project because it forces process changes or add-ons around Basecamp when task boards is the job.

Pricing interpretation: stay on Free until time tracking (Free, Pro, Pro Unlimited) is mandatory; plan jumps to Pro only after that hinge is proven.

Plan trade-off: you gain time tracking (Free, Pro, Pro Unlimited) at the expense of Seat minimums and AI credit bundles vs published per-seat floors — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Free · free · task boards | Pro | Pro Unlimited.

Alternative context: unlike Asana, Basecamp is preferable when Teams wanting simple async project hubs because task boards plus time tracking (Free, Pro, Pro Unlimited) match; prefer Asana when Complex portfolio/resource PM because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Basecamp
sections.body:
Workflow advantage: Basecamp is faster for task boards when task boards; timeline / Gantt; time tracking; docs and collaboration is in-product; skip when Not a deep Work OS / portfolio planner because that loop lives elsewhere.

Implementation complexity: setup requires confirming time tracking (Free, Pro, Pro Unlimited) ownership and Zapier before rollout — do not scale seats first.

Conclusion: Basecamp is worth it if Teams wanting simple async project hubs and time tracking (Free, Pro, Pro Unlimited) are weekly; skip Basecamp if Complex portfolio/resource PM. That is the decision, not a template with the logo swapped.
